details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
vt. 喂养; 满足（欲望等）; 向…提供; 供…作食物
vi. 吃，以…为食; 流入，注入，进入（如油流入机器）; [电子学]馈入
n. 饲料（尤指粗饲料），施肥; 喂送; 草料; （尤指向地方性电视台）馈送电视节目
时态：fed, feeding, feeds
分布：饲料(51%)，喂养(21%)，饲养(14%)，一餐(6%)，吃饲料(5%)，进餐(1%)，靠 ... 为生(1%)，向 ... 提供(1%)
→来自food的动词形式。
v.(on,with)喂养,饲养;(with)向...供给I feed the food to the bleeding man in the flood.我把食品喂给洪水中的那个流血的人.
verb (fed, fed)
GIVE FOOD 给予食物
ESSENTIAL transitive
■to give food to a person, group or animal 给（人、团体或动物）提供食物；喂养
•I usually feed the neighbour's cat while she's away.邻居不在家时，我经常替她喂猫。
•Let's feed the kids first and have our dinner after.我们先喂饱孩子，然后再吃饭吧。
•[+ two objects] Do you feed your chickens corn?你给鸡喂玉米吗？
•If you feed your dog on cakes and biscuits, it's not surprising he's so fat.如果你是用蛋糕和饼干喂狗，它长这么肥就不奇怪了。
•The kids love feeding bread to the ducks.那些孩子喜欢给鸭子喂面包。
intransitive or transitive
■If a baby or animal feeds, it eats or drinks milk （婴儿或动物）吃奶
•The baby only feeds once a night at the moment, thank goodness.感谢老天，宝宝现在每晚只吃一次奶。
•[R] Most babies can feed them selves by the time they're a year old.多数婴儿到一岁的时候就可以自己吃东西了。
transitive
■to be enough food for a group of people or animals 足够（人或动物）食用
•This amount of pasta won't feed ten people.这些义大利面不够十个人吃。
transitive
■to produce or supply enough food for someone or something 为…提供食物；养活
•[R] If agriculture were given priority, the country would easily be able to feed it self.如果优先发展农业，这个国家很容易就能实现自给自足。
•Feed the world/starving.养活全世界／饥饿的人。
transitive
■to give a plant substances that will help it grow 为（植物）施肥
•Don't forget to feed the tomatoes.别忘了为番茄施肥。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
PUT 放置
intransitive or transitive [usually + adv/prep]
■to supply something to a person or thing, or put something into a machine or system, especially in a regular or continuous way 供给；供应；（尤指规律地或连续地）把…放进（机器或系统）
•The vegetables are fed into the machine at this end.蔬菜从这头放进机器里。
•The images are fed over satellite networks to broadcasters throughout the world.图像透过卫星网路传送给全世界的广播公司。
•[+ two objects] A member of the princess's staff had been feeding the newspaper information/feeding information to the newspaper.公主的一名工作人员过去一直向这家报社提供消息。
•Several small streams feed into (= join) the river near here.几条小溪在附近汇流注入该河。
transitive
■to put fuel on or inside something that burns, to keep it burning 添（燃料）
•Remember to feed the fire while I'm out.我不在时记得给火添柴。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
a feeding frenzy
■a situation when people try to get as much information as possible about an event, or to make as much profit as they can from it, especially in an unpleasant way （尤指以令人不快的方式）试图获取某事的资讯，或借助某事谋取最大利益
•Her sudden death sparked off a feeding frenzy in the media.她突然离世，引发媒体蜂拥而至，进行采访。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
be like feeding time at the zoo humorous
■to be very noisy and untidy and have no order 喧闹混乱
•Tea-time in our house is like feeding time at the zoo!我们家吃茶点时就像动物园里喂食时一样，到处闹哄哄的。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
feed sb a line disapproving
■to tell someone something that is not completely true, often as an excuse 以不实之词欺骗（某人），向（某人）虚报情况
•She fed me a line about not having budgeted for pay increases this year.她骗我说今年的预算中没有涨工资这一项。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
feed sb to the lions
■to force someone to do something unpleasant or dangerous that they do not want to do 迫使（某人）做危险或令人不悦的事
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
Phrasal Verbs feed off/on sth
■to increase because of something, or to use something to succeed or get advantages 因…而增长；利用…取得成功（或优势）
•Fascism feeds off poverty.贫穷助长了法西斯主义。
[fi:d] verb (fed, fed)
Phrasal Verbs [M] feed sb/sth up
■to make a person or animal healthier or fatter by giving them a lot of food 养壮；养肥
•You've lost a lot of weight - you need feeding up a bit.你瘦了很多，需要吃胖一点。
[fi:d] noun
FOOD 食物
countable UK (US feeding)
■when a baby has something to eat or drink （婴儿的）一餐
•The baby had a feed an hour ago, so she can't be hungry.宝宝一小时前刚喂过一次，所以她不可能是饿了。
uncountable
■food eaten by animals that are not kept as pets 动物饲料
•cattle/animal feed牛／动物饲料
⇒ See also chickenfeed
countable old-fashioned
■a large meal 丰盛的一餐
[fi:d] noun
MACHINE PART 机器部分
countable
■the part of a machine through which it is supplied with fuel or with something else that it needs （机器的）进料装置，进料器
•the car's oil feed汽车的供油管道
•the printer's paper feed印表机的进纸装置
graze, nourish, feed
这组词都有“提供所需食物，喂养”的意思，其区别是：
graze: 侧重指用正在生长的青草喂养牲畜。
nourish: 指提供生长、健康或维持生存所必需的食物或养料，尤指用营养品促进生长。
feed: 普通用词，含义广泛。既可指给人或动物提供食物，又可指给植物以养料或为机器等加燃料等。
enhance, raise, feed
enhance: 增强，提高，美化（多用于抽象意义）
raise: 养育（孩子），饲养（家畜），生产（作物）,提高，上升，养育
feed: 给（人或动物）食物
vt. 喂养；供给；放牧；抚养（家庭等）；靠…为生
- grass, take care of, range
vi. 吃东西；流入
- take food, flow into
n. [畜牧] 饲料；饲养；（动物或婴儿的）一餐
- meal, breeding, husbandry

entries.meaning: n.反馈；反馈意见
entries.example:
Did you get any feedback from your clients?
你从顾客那儿得到什么反馈了吗?

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Did you get any feedback from your clients?
你从顾客那儿得到什么反馈了吗?

The writer gets no immediate feedback and simply has to imagine the reader's reaction.
作者没有得到及时的反馈,只能猜测读者的反应。

Try to give each student some feedback on the task.
针对这项作业,尽量给每位学生提出反馈意见。

I'd appreciate some feedback on my work.
如果有人对我的工作提出意见我将感激不尽。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 反馈; 反应; 反馈噪音
分布：反馈(95%)，反馈意见(5%)
→即喂回来。
n.反馈;反应;回授
【记】feed（v 喂养），back反－反馈
noun uncountable
OPINION 意见
ADVANCED
■information or statements of opinion about something, such as a new product, that provide an idea of whether it is successful or liked 回馈资讯，回馈意见
•Have you had any feedback from customers about the new soap?有关新款肥皂你有没有收到顾客的回馈意见？
•positive/negative feedback正面的／负面的回馈意见
['fi:d.bæk] noun uncountable
MACHINE 机器
■the sudden, high, unpleasant noise sometimes produced by an amplifier when sound it produces is put back into it （扩音器的）回馈噪音
•Jimi Hendrix loved to fling his guitar around to get weird and wonderful sounds from the feedback.吉米‧罕醉克斯喜欢用力弹拨他的吉他，这样扬声器的啸声中就会传出一种怪诞奇妙的声音。
■specialized
■the return back into a machine or system of part of what it produces, especially to improve what is produced 回馈（把机器或系统生产之物的一部份再度投进机器或系统的做法，此举多用以改良生产物）
•Feedback from the sensors ensures that the car engine runs smoothly.侦测器的回馈能确保汽车引擎平稳运转。
n. [电子] [自] 反馈；成果，资料；回复
- production, outcome, information

entries.meaning:
n.感觉；知觉；气氛；鉴赏力；反感
adj.有感情的；富于同情心的；含情脉脉的
（复）feelings：感情.
entries.example:
I have a feeling that we are being followed.
我有种感觉我们正被人跟踪。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
I have a feeling that we are being followed.
我有种感觉我们正被人跟踪。

The feeling deepened with the passing of the years.
这种感觉一年一年地加深了。

He had no movement or feeling below his navel.
肚脐以下没有知觉，也不能活动。

I've lost all feeling in the left arm.
我左臂完全失去了知觉。

There is a weird feeling about the place.
这地方有一种神秘的气氛。

You have no feeling for the beauty of nature.
你对大自然的美缺乏欣赏力。

His speech caused a lot of feeling.
他的讲演引起了很多反感。

His rapid promotion caused much bad feeling among his colleagues.
他获迅速提升在同事中引起很大的不满。

He is not a mere lump of clay but a feeling creature.
他不仅具有血肉之躯而且是一个有感情的人。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 感觉，知觉，情绪; 感情; 气氛
adj. 富有感情的，有感觉的; 有同情心的，仁慈的
v. 感觉; 认为(feel的现在分词)
分布：感觉(81%)，知觉(6%)，气氛(5%)，富于同情心的(2%)，鉴赏力(2%)，含情脉脉的(2%)，反感(1%)，有感情的(1%)
感情(feel感觉)[-ing 1.表名词"状态"2.表名词"行业"3.表形容词"正…的","令人…的"]
n.感情;心情;知觉;同情I've lost all feeling in the left arm.我左臂完全失去了知觉.
noun
PHYSICAL SENSE 感官
ESSENTIAL countable or uncountable
■when you feel something physical （感官的）感觉
•I had a tingling feeling in my fingers.我手指感到刺痛。
•I've got this strange feeling in my stomach.我的胃里有种怪怪的感觉。
•My toes were so cold that I'd lost all feeling in them.我的脚趾冻得完全失去知觉了。
['fi:.lɪŋ] noun
EMOTION 情绪
ESSENTIAL countable or uncountable
■emotion 感情；感触；情绪
•The feeling of loneliness suddenly overwhelmed him.一种孤独感突然涌上他的心头。
•There's a feeling of dissatisfaction with the government.存在着对政府的不满情绪。
•[+ that] I got the feeling that I was not welcome.我感觉到我不受欢迎。
•Her performance seemed to me completely lacking in feeling.在我看来她的表演完全缺乏感情。
feelings [plural]
ADVANCED
■emotions, especially those influenced by other people （尤指受他人影响而产生的）情感，感情
•Some people say that dogs have feelings.有人说狗是有感情的。
•I wanted to spare his feelings (= not to upset him) , so I didn't tell him what she'd said about him.我不想惹他难受，所以没告诉他她是怎么说他的。
['fi:.lɪŋ] noun
OPINION 意见
IMPROVER countable
■opinion 意见
•My feeling is that we had better act quickly or it will be too late.我的意见是我们最好快点行动，否则就太迟了。
['fi:.lɪŋ] noun
bad feeling UK (US bad feelings)
■when people are upset or angry with each other 恶感；不满；反感
•I'd like to complain to the neighbours about the noise, but I don't want to cause any bad feeling (between us).我想去向邻居抱怨太吵了，但又不想（在我们之间）闹出任何不愉快。
['fi:.lɪŋ] noun
hurt sb's feelings
■to upset someone by criticizing them or by refusing something that they have offered you 伤害（某人）的感情
sensation, feeling, perception, sense
这组词都有“感觉”的意思，其区别是：
sensation: 系较严密的科学用词，指听觉、味觉、视觉、嗅觉或触觉；还可指引起激动或轰动的事物。
feeling: 最普通用词，既可指身体上的感觉，如冷暖、饥饿、疼痛等，又可指精神上的感觉，如喜、怒、哀、乐、失望等。
perception: 侧重对外界刺激的反应和对产生感觉的物体的辨别。
sense: 主要指人或动物身体上的感觉。复数形式指人的知觉。
sentiment, sensation, feeling, passion, emotion
这组词都有“感情”的意思，其区别是：
sentiment: n.思想感情，情绪，感情色彩，指由于某种思想唤起的感情，强调主观作用，有时候也带有理智成分。
• When our grandmother died, we remembered her life with strong sentiment. 当祖母逝世时，我们深深地怀念她的一生。
sensation: n.指人体感官受到外部刺激时产生的感觉，知觉。
• When she watched the film, she had the sensation that she was in a moving car. 她看电影时，感觉自己正坐在一辆开动的汽车上。
feeling: n.指一般的情绪、感觉，它一般不反映感情的本质和强度。
passion: n.激情，热情，欲望，极度的仇恨，指强烈的爱好、愤怒或情欲。
• He spoke with passion about the love of freedom. 他满腔热情地谈论着对自由的热爱。
emotion: n.情感，感情，指喜怒哀乐等较激动的情绪，表示某物引起的激动。
• He felt mixed emotions when he thought of her. 当他想起她时便产生一种复杂的感情。
sentiment, affection, feeling, passion, emotion
这组词都有“感情”的意思，其区别是：
sentiment: 一般指由一种思想激起的感情，含较大的理智因素。
affection: 指对人的爱慕或深厚、温柔的感情。
feeling: 普通用词，含义广。多指具体的或内心的感受，或表露出来的强烈情感。
passion: 指极强烈的感情、尤指愤怒、爱好等。也常指两性间的爱情。
emotion: 普通用词，词义中性。泛指因外界刺激而引起思想情感从细微变化到最强烈的发作。
n. [生理] 感觉，触觉； [心理] 感情，情绪；同情
- mood, consciousness, emotion, affection, spirit
adj. 有感觉的；有同情心的；富于感情的
- caring
v. [生理] 感觉；认为（feel的现在分词）；触摸
- sensing, handling

entries.meaning:
n.家伙；同事；同伴；研究员；校董

entries.example:
Jack is a clever fellow indeed.
杰克确实是个聪明的家伙。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Jack is a clever fellow indeed.
杰克确实是个聪明的家伙。

I can't tolerate that rude fellow.
我不能容忍那个粗鲁的家伙。

That foolish fellow is looking for trouble.
那个愚蠢的家伙在自找麻烦。

他虽然脾气暴躁,但是一个很好的同事。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 同伴; 男子; （大学的）研究员; （某些学院或大学的）董事
adj. 同伴的; 同事的; 同类的; 同情况的
vt. 使…与另一个对等; 使…与另一个匹敌
分布：家伙(60%)，同事(14%)，同伴(6%)，研究员(5%)，同事的(5%)，同伴的(5%)，同类的(4%)，校董(1%)
→来自古英语feolaga, 同伴，合作者。feo-,同fee, 古义金钱，laga-, 同lay, 放置。即合伙做事情的人，同伴。
n.人,家伙;伙伴,同事a.同样的,同事的The fellow's yellow pillow is hollowed by his follower.那个家伙的黄色枕头被他的跟随者掏空了.
US [-oʊ] adjective [before noun]
IMPROVER
■describes someone who has the same job or interests as you, or is in the same situation as you 同事的；同伴的；同情况的
•She introduced me to some of her fellow students.她把我介绍给她的几位同班同学。
•Our fellow travellers were mostly Spanish-speaking tourists.和我们同行的旅伴大多是讲西班牙语的游客。
UK ['fel.əʊ] US [-oʊ] noun countable
MAN 人 informal
■a man, used especially in the past by people in a higher social class 人，男人，家伙（尤为旧时社会阶层较高的人使用）
•He seemed like a decent sort of a fellow.他似乎是个正派的人。
UK ['fel.əʊ] US [-oʊ] noun countable
MEMBER 成员
■a member of a group of high-ranking teachers at a particular college or university or of particular academic societies （学院或大学的）研究员；（学术协会的）会员
•Georgia's a fellow of Clare College, Cambridge.乔治亚是剑桥大学卡莱尔学院的研究员。
■a member of an official organization for a particular subject or job （官方机构的）成员
•He's a fellow of the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors.他是皇家特许测量师协会的会员。
comrade, companion, colleague, partner, fellow, associate
这组词都有“同事，伙伴”的意思，其区别是：
comrade: 指具有共同的事业、利益关系相一致的人。
companion: 指陪伴他人的人，即同伴或陪伴。
colleague: 一般用于对同事的正式称呼，基本上专用在职业关系上。
partner: 指事业中处于合伙关系的人，或指婚姻、游戏、跳舞中的另一方。
fellow: 多用复数形式，指一块住、生活或同行共事的人。
associate: 普通用词，侧重指在利害关系上密切相关。
n. 家伙；朋友；同事；会员
- apple, customer, friend, member, guy
adj. 同伴的，同事的；同道的

details.text:

adjective
SEX 性别
ESSENTIAL
■belonging or relating to women, or the sex that can give birth to young or produce eggs 女性的；妇女的；雌的；母的
•She was voted the best female vocalist.她当选最佳女歌手。
•Female lions do not have manes.母狮没有鬃毛。
⇒ See also feminine
■describes plants which produce flowers that will later develop into fruit （植物）能结果实的
['fi:.meɪl] adjective
CONNECTING PART 连接部分 specialized
■describes a piece of equipment that has a hole or space into which another part can be fitted （设备）阴的，内孔的
•a female plug/connector母插头／内孔式连接器
Compare male
['fi:.meɪl] noun countable
IMPROVER
■a female animal or person 雌性动物；女子
•The kitten was actually a female, not a male.这只小猫的确是母的，不是公的。
•Females (= women) represent 40% of the country's workforce.女性占全国劳动力的40%。
■used to refer to a woman in a way that shows no respect 女人（不尊重的说法）
•I suspect the doctor thought I was just another hysterical female.我猜那个医生认为我只不过是另一个歇斯底里的女人罢了。
female, woman, lady
这组词都有“女性”的意思，其区别是：
female: 与male“男(性)的，公的，雄的”相对，强调性别，可指人或动物，但除用于科学和统计上外，大多含贬义。
woman: 与man相对，侧重成年妇女的特点，系成年妇女的通称。
lady: 与gentleman相对，强调所谓高贵的气质、品德和教养等。也指对女性的礼貌称呼。
female, feminine
这组词都有“女性的”的意思，其区别是：
female: 仅指性别的分类，指人、动物或植物，甚至无生命的东西均可。
feminine: 强调女性所特有的或同女性有关的特质、特征。
adj. 女性的； [生物] 雌性的；柔弱的，柔和的
- delicate, feminine
n. 女人； [植] [动] 雌性动物
- she, jenny

entries.meaning:
n.栅栏；围墙；买卖赃物的人
v.用篱笆围住；束缚；击剑；回避
entries.example:
He tried to see over the fence but it was too high.
他试图从栅栏上面看过去，但它太高了。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
He tried to see over the fence but it was too high.
他试图从栅栏上面看过去，但它太高了。

He hired a workman to repair the fence.
他雇用了一个工人修理围墙。

That fence is the limit of the schoolyard.
那堵围墙是校园的界限。

The loot had disappeared and been handled by a fence.
赃物失踪后被一个销脏的人处理掉了。

One end of the garden was fenced off for chickens.
花园的一端已用篱笆隔开来养鸡。

She felt fenced in by domestic routine.
她觉得自己完全被家务事束缚住了。

I should like the chance to fence with a worthier opponent.
我希望有机会跟实力相当的对手击剑。

I'll fence with you if you wish.
如果你愿意，我就和你击剑。

It is not manly for you to fence off the consequences of your action.
你要是回避你的行动后果，就不像个男子汉。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 栅栏，篱笆; 围墙; 防护物; 剑术
vt. 用篱笆围住; 防护; 练习剑术
vi. 练习击剑; 搪塞; 围以栅栏; 跳过栅栏
时态：fenced, fencing, fences
分布：栅栏(64%)，围墙(22%)，击剑(6%)，买卖赃物的人(3%)，用篱笆围住(3%)，回避(1%)，束缚(1%)
→缩写自defence或defense, 挡开。引申义击剑，篱笆等。
n.篱笆;围栏;剑术v.用篱笆瓦围住;击剑The offensive offender defended himself with the fence.那个讨厌的触犯者用篱笆自卫.
noun countable
STRUCTURE 结构
IMPROVER
■a structure which divides two areas of land, similar to a wall but made of wood or wire and supported with posts 栅栏；篱笆；围栏
[fents] noun countable
CRIMINAL 罪犯 old-fashioned slang
■a person who buys and sells stolen goods 买卖赃物的人
[fents] verb intransitive
■to fight as a sport with a long thin sword 击剑
[fents] verb intransitive
Phrasal Verbs [M] fence sth in
■to build a fence around an area 用栅栏（或篱笆）围住
•She would need to fence in the field if she was to keep a horse there.如果她打算在那里养一匹马，就必须用栅栏把那块地围起来。
[fents] verb intransitive
Phrasal Verbs [often passive] fence sb in informal
■to limit someone's activity in an annoying or discouraging way 限制（某人）的自由，束缚
•I feel a bit fenced in at work because my boss won't let me apply for promotion.我觉得工作上有点受压制，因为老板不准我申请升职。
[fents] verb intransitive
Phrasal Verbs [M] fence sth off
■to separate an area with a fence in order to stop people or animals from entering it 用栅栏（或篱笆）隔开
•The hill had been fenced off to stop animals grazing on it.已经用栅栏把那座山隔开，以防止动物吃那里的草。
fence, hedge
这组词都有“篱笆”的意思，其区别是：
fence: 指为阻止人或牲畜等进入田地或院子等而用树木、铁丝网、栅栏等筑成篱笆样的东西。
hedge: 主要指利用灌木丛构成的篱笆。
enclose, fence, encircle, surround, envelop
这组词都有“包围”的意思，其区别是：
enclose: 指把某物四周围住或封闭起来，使之与外界隔绝。
fence: 通常指用栅栏栏开或围起来。
encircle: 侧重在某事物周围围成圈状。
surround: 普通用词，既可指环绕、围绕，也可指军事上的包围。
envelop: 着重指把某个物体完全包起来或整个封起来。
n. 栅栏；围墙；剑术
- bounding wall, perimeter wall
vt. 防护；用篱笆围住；练习剑术
- defend, forefend
vi. 击剑；搪塞；围以栅栏；跳过栅栏
- prevaricate, tergiversate

entries.meaning: adj.肥沃的；富饶的；能繁殖的；多产的；（创造力）丰富的
entries.example:
There are fertile fields in the Nile Delta.
尼罗河三角洲土地肥沃。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
There are fertile fields in the Nile Delta.
尼罗河三角洲土地肥沃。

We have irrigated the desert area to make it fertile.
我们已经灌溉了荒芜地区使它肥沃。

It was a pleasant fertile spot, well wooded and rich in pasture.
那是一个富饶的，使人愉快的地方，材木苍然，牧草丰富。

This fertile land bears the hopes of the farmers.
这块富饶的土地,孕育着庄稼人的希望！

Tilapia are very fertile, and reproduce several offspring every year.
罗非鱼一年能够繁殖数代,生殖能力很强。

The rotation of crops keeps the soil healthy and fertile.
谷物轮种使土壤保持了肥力和高质。

His paper was remarkably simple and fertile.
他的评论异常简单而且内容丰富。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
adj. 肥沃的; 可繁殖的; 想象力丰富的
分布：肥沃的(77%)，富饶的(16%)，多产的(6%)，能繁殖的(1%)
→来自词根fer,带来，携带，词源同bring, infer. 引申词义肥沃的，多产的。
肥沃的;多产的(fert[=fer]+ile→能带来粮食→肥沃的)[fer=bring,carry,表示"带来,拿来"]
肥沃的(fert带有;繁殖+ile)[-ile 1.表形容词"…的"2.表名词"物体"]
a.肥沃的,富饶的;能繁殖的Utilize the fertilizer to keep the land fertile.利用化肥保持土地肥沃.
US ['fɝ:.tˌəl] adjective
LAND 土地
ADVANCED
■describes land that can produce a large number of good quality crops 肥沃的；富饶的 Compare barren
UK ['fɜ:.taɪl] US ['fɝ:.tˌəl] adjective
PEOPLE/ANIMALS/PLANTS 人／动物／植物
ADVANCED
■describes animals or plants that are able to produce (a lot of) young or fruit （动物或植物）可繁殖的，能生育的，能结果的
•People get less fertile as they get older.随着年龄增长，人的生育能力逐渐下降。
Opposite infertile describes a seed or egg that is able to develop into a new plant or animal 受粉的；受精的，受孕的
UK ['fɜ:.taɪl] US ['fɝ:.tˌəl] adjective
IMAGINATION 想像力的
■A fertile mind or imagination is active and produces a lot of interesting and unusual ideas. 想像力丰富的；点子多的
UK ['fɜ:.taɪl] US ['fɝ:.tˌəl] adjective
fertile ground for sth
■a situation or place which produces good results or a lot of ideas …的沃土
•British politics remains very fertile ground for comedy.英国政治依然为喜剧提供丰富的素材。
adj. 富饶的，肥沃的； [植] 能生育的
- rich, viable
n. 肥沃，多产
- pregnancy, enrichment

entries.meaning: n.肥料
entries.example:
The stalks will rot and make good fertilizer.
杆儿腐烂后会成为很好的肥料。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
The stalks will rot and make good fertilizer.
杆儿腐烂后会成为很好的肥料。

Crushed bones make one of the best fertilizers.
碎骨是最好的肥料之一。

Farmers bartered rice for fertilizer.
农民们用大米换肥料。

The tractor hauled the fertilizer away.
拖拉机把肥料拉走了。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 肥料，化肥; 受精媒介物; 促进发展者
分布：肥料(100%)
肥料(来自fertilize)[fer=bring,carry,表示"带来,拿来"]
n.(fertiliser)肥料Utilize the fertilizer to keep the land fertile.利用化肥保持土地肥沃.
US ['fɝ:.tˌəl.aɪ-] noun countable or uncountable
■a natural or chemical substance which is spread on the land or given to plants, to make plants grow well 肥料
•organic fertilizer有机肥料
•a liquid/chemical fertilizer液体肥料／化肥
n. [肥料] 肥料；受精媒介物；促进发展者
- manure

entries.meaning:
adj.节日的；喜庆的
n.节日；欢宴；庆祝及祭祀
entries.example:
We all wore festival costumes to the ball.
我们都穿著节日的盛装去参加舞会。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
We all wore festival costumes to the ball.
我们都穿著节日的盛装去参加舞会。

We all immersed in the gaiety of the Spring Festival.
我们都沉浸在春节的欢乐之中。

The Nadam Festival is a traditional occasion for Mongols to get together for a few days of festivity.
传统地，蒙古国人民在那达慕节要聚集欢宴几天。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 节日; 节期; 贺宴，会演
adj. 节日的，喜庆的
分布：节日(84%)，节日的(11%)，喜庆的(3%)，欢宴(1%)，庆祝及祭祀(1%)
→来自拉丁语festa, 假日，宗教节日，来自dhes, 神，与神和宗教相关的，词源同festival, fan, theist.词义由祭祀，庆祝，狂欢引申为盛宴等。
节目,宴会(fext+ival表名词成形容词)[fest=feast,表示"节目"]
n.节日;音乐节;戏剧节a.节日的;快乐的During the festival the investor investigated his ancestor.节日期间投资者调查了他的祖宗.
noun countable
IMPROVER
■a special day or period, usually in memory of a religious event, with its own social activities, food or ceremonies 节日；节期
•a Jewish/Christian/Hindu festival犹太教／基督教／印度教节日
IMPROVER
■an organized set of special events, such as musical performances （音乐等的）会演，节
•a folk/pop/rock festival民间音乐／流行音乐／摇滚音乐节
•The Brighton Festival is held every year around May time.布莱顿艺术节每年五月份左右举行。
•the Cannes Film Festival坎城电影节
holiday, leave, vacation, festival
这组词都有“假日，节日”的意思，其区别是：
holiday: 指按规定不工作的各种假日，时间可长可短。在英国复数形式表示较长的假期。
leave: 主要指政府机关工作人员或军队人员获准的休假、假期。
vacation: 通常指时间较长的假期，如学校的寒暑假等。
festival: 指公众庆祝、欢度的节日。
n. 节日；庆祝，纪念活动；欢乐
- holiday, joy, celebration
adj. 节日的，喜庆的；快乐的
- cheerful, enjoyable

entries.meaning:
vt.取来；卖得；给（某人）一击
n.取得
entries.example:
Fetch me the tape from my drawer.
请把我抽屉里的磁带取来。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Fetch me the tape from my drawer.
请把我抽屉里的磁带取来。

Shall I fetch your coat for you?
我去把上衣给你取来好吗?

This house should fetch a good price.
这所房子应该卖个好价钱。

The picture should fetch 2000 pounds at auction.
这张画拍卖可得2000英镑。

She fetched him a terrific slap in the face.
她狠狠地给了他一记耳光。

Hence, the system needs to fetch the needed data as soon as possible.The existing way is based on file prefetching.
因此若要降低使用者等待时间，则需加快反应时间，必须尽早取得档案资料。

His sale is certain to fetch a good price on the transfer market which will expand the club's budget for signing new talent during January.
他的售卖在将会为在一月期间签署新的才能扩张俱乐部的预算的移动市场上对取得善行价格是确定的。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
vt. 接来（某人）; 使发出; 吸引; 售得（若干价钱）
vi. 抵达，到达; 取来; 卖得（好价钱）
n. 拿取，拿来; 诡计; 风浪区
时态：fetched, fetching, fetches
分布：取来(56%)，卖得(25%)，取得(19%)
→fet, 同foot, 脚。即跑腿。
v.取来;接来;引出;售得;吸引n.取得;拿When I fetched the sketch on the stretcher I found the secretary's secret.当我拿来担架上的素描时我发现了秘书的秘密.
verb
GET 拿取
IMPROVER transitive
■to go to another place to get something or someone and bring them back （去）拿来，取回；（去）请来
•[+ two objects] Could you fetch me my glasses/fetch my glasses for me from the other room, please?你去另一个房间帮我把眼镜拿过来好吗？
•I have to fetch my mother from the station.我要去车站接我母亲。
[fetʃ] verb
SELL 卖
transitive
■to be sold for a particular amount of money 售得，卖得（…价钱）
•The paintings fetched over a million dollars.这些油画卖了100多万美元。
•The house didn't fetch as much as she was hoping it would.房子没有卖到她期望的那个价钱。
[fetʃ] verb
HIT 打
transitive + two objects old-fashioned informal
■to hit someone with the hand （用手）打（某人）
•I fetched him a smart blow on the ear!我狠狠地给了他一记耳光。
[fetʃ] verb
fetch and carry for sb
■to do boring, unskilled jobs for someone, as if you were their servant 为（某人）打杂，为（某人）当听差，为（某人）跑腿
[fetʃ] verb
Phrasal Verbs fetch up mainly US informal
■to arrive somewhere, especially without intending to 偶然来到，意外到达
•After a whole hour of driving, we fetched up back where we started.开车开了整整一小时后，我们竟然又回到了出发地。
convey, fetch, get, transport, take, bring, carry
这组词都有“带、拿、取”的意思，其区别是：
convey: 指通过中间人传递信息，或以某种方式把人或物送到目的地。
fetch: 指一往一返，相当于go and bring，去取了东西或带人再返回到出发处。
get: 口语用词，与fetch基本同义，语气随便。
transport: 指使用车辆或机械设备把人或货物从一处运载到另一处。
take: 指从说话人或说话人心目中所在处把某人或某物带离开，带到离说话者有一定距离的地方，与bring的方向正相反，侧重方向，不着重方式。
bring: 指从某处把人或物带到或拿到说话者所在的地点，强调方向，不着重方式。
carry: 指把物品从一个地方带到另一个地方，不涉及方向，只强调方式。
vt. 取来；接来；到达；吸引
- absorb, attract, engage, draw, strike
vi. 拿；取物；卖得
- take
n. 取得；诡计
- taking, procurement, scheme, fraud

entries.meaning:
n.狂热；发烧；发热
v.（使）发烧；（使）狂热
entries.example:
Football fever gripped the town when the local team reached the cup final.
在当地的足球队打进了优胜杯的决赛圈后，全市掀起一阵足球热。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Football fever gripped the town when the local team reached the cup final.
在当地的足球队打进了优胜杯的决赛圈后，全市掀起一阵足球热。

War fever was rising all over the Middle East.
战争狂热正在整个中东地区升温。

Her fever lasted five days without intermission.
她连续五天一直发烧。

My fever is gone, but I still have a cough.
我不发烧了，但还是有点咳嗽。

Flu is an infectious disease characterized by fever, aches and pains and exhaustion.
流感是一种传染病，其特征是发热、全身疼痛和疲乏无力。

Pneumonitis is usually associated with fever.
间质肺炎常伴有发热。

I feel as if I'm running a fever.
我好像有点儿发热。

He went to see a doctor at the onset of a fever.
他开始发烧时便去看医生了。

Fever is one manifestation of a cold.
发烧是受凉的一种表现。

War fever was rising all over the Middle East.
战争狂热正在整个中东地区升温。

Soon he succumbed to silver mining fever.
没过多久他就被开采银矿的狂热所感染。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 发热，发烧; 热病; 一时的狂热; 激动不安
vt. 引起发热; 使狂热; 使患热病
vi. 发热或变得发热; 狂热; 患热病
分布：发烧(71%)，发热(18%)，狂热(11%)
→来自拉丁语febris, 发烧，来自dhegh, 燃烧，词源同day,febrile.
n.发热,狂热However, Lever never fevers; nevertheless, he is clever forever.无论如何,杠杆从未发烧;尽管如此,他始终机灵.
US [-vɚ] noun
ILLNESS 疾病
ADVANCED countable or uncountable
■a medical condition in which the body temperature is higher than usual and the heart beats very fast 发烧，发热
•He's got a headache and a slight fever.他头痛，还有点发烧。
UK ['fi:.vər] US [-vɚ] noun
EXCITEMENT 激动
uncountable
■a state of great excitement 激动，狂热，兴奋
•The whole country seems to be in the grip of football fever.全国似乎都陷入了对足球的狂热中。
fever, heat
这组词都有“热，热度”的意思，其区别是：
fever: 通常指超过正常体温所出现的发烧、发热；可引申指情绪的激昂和兴奋。
heat: 一般指具体的热、热度、热力等，有时也应热情、激动的感情。
n. [医] 发烧， [临床] 发热；狂热
- abandon, febricity
vt. [医] 使发烧；使狂热；使患热病
- fanaticize
vi. [医] 发烧；狂热；患热病
- run a temperature, go wild

entries.meaning: n.纤维；质地；性情
entries.example:
The ribbon of the rifle is fabricated with fibre.
来复枪的带子是用纤维制作的。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
The ribbon of the rifle is fabricated with fibre.
来复枪的带子是用纤维制作的。

Scientists are recommending that people eat more fibre.
科学家建议人们多吃些纤维素。

He is a man of real fibre.
他是一个有骨气的男子。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 纤维; 性格; 硬纸板纤维板
分布：纤维(98%)，质地(1%)，性情(1%)
US [-bɚ] noun
THREAD 线
ADVANCED countable
■any of the thread-like parts which form plant or artificial material and which can be made into cloth （植物或人造物的）纤维，丝
•The fibres are woven into fabric.纤维被织成织物。
ADVANCED countable or uncountable
■threads when they are in a mass that can be used for making products such as cloth and rope （布、绳等的）纤维；纤维物质
•Natural fibres such as cotton tend to be cooler.棉类等天然纤维往往更凉爽。
•artificial/man-made/natural fibre人造／天然纤维
countable or uncountable
■one of various thread-like structures in the body, such as those found in muscle （人体组织的）纤维
•muscle fibre(s)肌肉纤维
UK (ALSO US fiber) UK ['faɪ.bər] US [-bɚ] noun
FOOD 食物
ADVANCED uncountable
■a substance in foods such as fruit, vegetables and brown bread, which travels through the body as waste and helps the contents of the bowels to pass through the body easily （水果、蔬菜、黑面包等中的）纤维素
•You should eat more dietary fibre to reduce the risk of bowel cancer.你应该多吃膳食纤维以降低患肠癌的风险。
UK (ALSO US fiber) UK ['faɪ.bər] US [-bɚ] noun
CHARACTER 性格
uncountable
■strength of character 品质；素质
•He lacked the moral fibre to be leader.品行方面他不具备当领导的素质。
UK (ALSO US fiber) UK ['faɪ.bər] US [-bɚ] noun
with every fibre of your being
■If you want or believe something with every fibre of your being, you want or believe it very much 一心一意；极其地
•She wanted to win the race with every fibre of her being.她一心想在赛跑中获胜。
n. [材] 纤维；纤维制品

entries.meaning: n.小说；虚构；杜撰
entries.example:
Real life is sometimes stranger than fiction.
现实生活有时比小说还离奇。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Real life is sometimes stranger than fiction.
现实生活有时比小说还离奇。

I like to read science fiction.
我喜欢读科幻小说。

It's important to distinguish fact from fiction.
把现实与虚构区分开来是很重要的。

His testimony is a complete fiction.
他的证言全是虚构。

Her cup was a fiction, but this is reality.
她的酒杯是杜撰出来的，但是这酒倒是真的。

As operating devices, perpetual-motion machines are the province of crackpot science and science fiction.
作为工作装置来看，永动机属于科学空想和科学上的杜撰。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 小说，虚构的文学作品; 虚构的或想像出的事，并非完全真实的事; 编造，虚构
分布：小说(85%)，虚构(13%)，杜撰(2%)
→来自dheigh, 捏造，制造，形成，词源同dough, figure. 用来指小说。
虚构;小说(fict+ion→做出的故事→小说)[fac,fact,fect,fic,fig=make,do,表示"做,制作"]
n.虚构,编造;小说In the fiction, the victim of the conflict pictured the picnic after victory.在小说中,冲突中的受害者描绘了胜利后的野餐.
【记】用fiction描述faction（n 派别；派系斗争；小派系；内讧）
noun
IMPROVER uncountable
■the type of book or story which is written about imaginary characters and events and not based on real people and facts 小说
•The book is a work of fiction and not intended as a historical account.这本书是一部小说作品而并非史实陈述。
•a writer of children's fiction儿童小说作家
countable or uncountable
■a false report or statement which you pretend is true 虚构的事；谎言
•[+ that] At work she kept up the fiction that she had a university degree.工作时，她一直谎称自己有大学学历。
•When he's telling you something, you never know what's fact and what's fiction.他向你叙事时，你永远都不知道哪些是事实，哪些是杜撰的。
story, tale, fiction, fable, romance, novel
这组词都有“小说，故事”的意思，其区别是：
story: 指篇幅较短，常包含一系列情节或事件，口述或书写成文的故事。
tale: 常可与story换用，指以事实为中心作叙述的故事，也指古代流传下来的传说故事或神话故事。
fiction: 指部分或全部虚构的短篇、中篇、长篇小说，也指传奇故事，是小说的总称。
fable: 指短小而寓有教育意义的虚构故事。故事的主人公多为拟人化的动物或非动物之类。也作传说解。
romance: 系novel早期的代用词，泛指具有强烈神话和传奇色彩的故事，现指爱情故事。
novel: 指任何有情节、人物、对白，虚构的长篇散文体故事。
n. 小说；虚构，编造；谎言
- invention, novel

entries.meaning:
n.田地；领域；运动场；场地；田野；JAVA中的范畴
vt.接球；派……上场；顺利处理
vi.担任外场员
adj.田间的；野外的
entries.example:
Many farmers are working in the fields.
许多农民在田里干活。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
Many farmers are working in the fields.
许多农民在田里干活。

He has become famous in his own field.
他在自己的领域里已经出名了。

The crowd cheered as the teams entered the field.
球队入场时观众们为之欢呼。

When Tom insulted the referee, he responded by ordering him off the field.
汤姆辱骂裁判员时,裁判员的反应是命令他退出场地。

Children went on a picnic and played in a field.
孩子们去野餐,在田野上嬉闹。

England will field a young side in the World Cup.
英国将派一支青年队参加世界杯。

The minister easily fielded all the journalist's awkward questions.
部长轻而易举地一一回答了记者提出的棘手问题。

Just before sunset the peasants quit laboring in the field.
农民们直到日落方结束在田间的劳动。

There are small holes in the balk of a field, where crabs and fish accumulate in the rainy season.
田间的梁木上有小洞口，螃蟹和鱼在雨季的时候会聚集在里面。

The plants are grown in a laboratory, then transplanted to a field.
这些植物是在实验室培育，然后再被移植到野外的。

The prospectors in the field obtain their information in many ways.
野外的勘探人员有许多办法来获取这些资料。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
n. 田; （作某种用途的）场地; （学习或研究的）领域; 运动场
vi. [棒球、板球等]担任外场员，担任守队队员; 接守，接防; 接，掷还（球）
adj. 实地的; [体育]1)。 在田赛场地进行的2)。 田赛的; 军事]野战的; 在实地工作的
vt. 保护; 把（农作物等）晒在场上; [棒球、板球等]按（或截）（球）; 即席圆满回答
时态：fielded, fielding, fields
分布：领域(55%)，田野(11%)，场地(10%)，运动场(8%)，田地(7%)，野外的(3%)，田间的(2%)，担任外场员(2%)，顺利处理(1%)，接球(1%)
→来自pele, 平的，展开，词源同plan, plat. 引申词义田野，领域等。
n.田野;运动场;(电或磁)场;领域,范围The unyielding man fiercely pierced the shield in the field.那个不屈的人凶猛地刺穿田野里的盾牌.
noun
LAND 土地
ESSENTIAL countable
■an area of land, used for growing crops or keeping animals, usually surrounded by a fence 田；地；牧场
•We drove past fields of ripening wheat.我们驱车经过快要成熟的麦田。
•The cows were all standing in one corner of the field.乳牛全都站在牧场的一角。
the field
■an area of land in which you are working or studying 实地，现场
•I spoke to an aid worker who had recently returned from the field.我和一位刚从现场归来的救援人员谈过。
[fi:ld] noun
SPORTS GROUND 运动场地
IMPROVER countable
■an area, usually covered with grass, used for playing sport （通常有草坪的）运动场
•the school playing/sports field学校运动场
•a football/hockey/rugby field足球／曲棍球／橄榄球场
take the field
■to go onto the field at the start of a game 登场，上场
•There were loud cheers as the Irish team took the field.爱尔兰队进场时欢呼声四起。
[fi:ld] noun
AREA OF INTEREST 兴趣领域
IMPROVER countable
■an area of activity or interest 界；领域；范围
•the field of history/science/medicine历史／科学／医学领域
•Are you still in the same field (= Are you doing the same type of work) ?你还在做老本行吗？
not be/be outside your field
■to be something you do not know much about 不是（某人）的专长
•Programming really isn't my field - you'd better ask Phil.程式设计真的不是我的专长，你最好问问菲尔。
[fi:ld] noun
COMPETITORS 竞争者
ADVANCED only singular [+ sing/pl verb]
■all the competitors taking part in a race or activity （参加比赛或活动的）全体运动员，全体人员
•The race started with a field of eleven, but two horses fell.比赛开始时有11匹马，但有两匹马摔倒了。
•We have a strong field this afternoon.今天下午我们阵容强大。
•Jones finished ahead of the field.琼斯率先到达终点。
[fi:ld] noun
COMPUTER 电脑
countable specialized
■a division of a database (= collection of similar information on a computer) which contains a particular type of information, such as names or numbers 信息组；栏位
[fi:ld] noun
sb's field of vision
■the whole area that someone can see （某人的）视线范围，视野，视场
[fi:ld] noun
leave the field clear for sb
■to stop competing with someone, making it possible for them to succeed 为（某人）的成功扫除障碍；为（某人）的胜利让路
•John decided not to apply for the job, which left the field clear for Emma.约翰决定不申请这份工作，这为艾玛扫除了障碍。
[fi:ld] verb
BALL 球
intransitive or transitive
■to catch or pick up the ball after it has been hit in a game such as cricket or baseball, and to try to prevent the other team from scoring （板球或棒球运动中）接（球），截（球），守（球），作守方
•He fielded the ball well.他稳稳地接住了球。
•Our team is fielding first.我们队先作守方。
[fi:ld] verb
ANSWER 回答
transitive
■to answer something cleverly or to avoid answering something directly 巧妙地回答
•He fielded some awkward questions very skilfully.他非常巧妙地回答了几个尴尬的问题。
[fi:ld] verb
TEAM 组织
transitive
■to have or produce a team of people to take part in an activity or event 使参加活动（或比赛）；组织参加
•The company fielded a group of experts to take part in the conference.公司组织了一个专家小组去参加会议。
field, territory, province, domain, sphere
这组词都有“范围，领域”的意思，其区别是：
field: 主要指经选定在一段时间内作专题研究的方面或领域，含夸张意味。
territory: 指科学知识、活动等的领域或范围。
province: 即可指科学、艺术、学问的领域或范围，又可指个人或机关职权的管辖范围。
domain: 指知识艺术、兴趣或人类活动的领域。
sphere: 指有明显分界线的范围或领域，强调彼此不会干扰、跨越，各不相关。
n. 领域；牧场；旷野；战场；运动场
- domain, province, territory, world, kingdom, universe
adj. 扫描场；田赛的；野生的
- wild, feral

entries.meaning: adj.强烈的；凶猛的；酷烈的
entries.example:
What he said met with fierce opposition.
他的话语遭到激烈反对。

details.title: 例句
details.text:
What he said met with fierce opposition.
他的话语遭到激烈反对。

Because there is so much unemployment, the competition for jobs is fierce.
因为失业严重，求职的竞争十分激烈。

The postman was bitten by a fierce dog.
那个邮递员被一只恶狗咬了。

He has a very fierce look on his face.
他脸上一副凶相。

The fierce sun parched the bare earth.
灼热的阳光炙烤着光秃秃的大地。

details.title: 卡片背面 · 词典摘录
details.text:
adj. 凶猛的，残忍的; 猛烈的; 狂热的
级别：fiercer, fiercest
分布：凶猛的(70%)，强烈的(27%)，酷烈的(3%)
→词源同feral, ferocity.
a.凶猛的,残忍的;狂热的,强烈的The unyielding man fiercely pierced the shield in the field.那个不屈的人凶猛地刺穿田野里的盾牌.
US [fɪrs] adjective
IMPROVER
■physically violent and frightening 猛烈的；激烈的；骇人的
•a fierce attack/battle猛烈的进攻／激烈的战斗
•Two men were shot during fierce fighting last weekend.上周末的激战中两人被枪击。
IMPROVER
■strong and powerful 狂暴的
•Fierce winds/seas prevented the race from taking place.狂风／汹涌的海浪致使比赛无法进行。
•Fire fighters had to retreat from the fierce heat.消防员面对逼人的热浪只好后撤。
IMPROVER
■showing strong feeling or energetic activity 强烈的；狂热的
•The expansion plans will face fierce opposition/resistance from environmentalists.扩建计划会遭到环境保护主义者的强烈反对／抵制。
•There is fierce competition to join the Special Branch.加入政治保安处要面对激烈的竞争。
■US informal
■difficult 难的
•The chemistry exam was fierce!化学考试太难了！
UK [fɪəs] US [fɪrs] adjective
something fierce US informal
■very much 很，非常
•I need a cold drink something fierce.我真想来杯冷饮。
stormy, wild, fierce, turbulent, violent
这组词都有“剧烈的，凶猛的，狂暴的”的意思，其区别是：
stormy: 指风雨大作，也指人很激动的感情。
wild: 普通用词，既可指自然界的荒芜，未被驯化状态，又指人的无法无天，不文明的野蛮行为。
fierce: 普通用词，指人或兽的凶猛残酷。
turbulent: 正式用词，多用描写风和水，也可指心神不定或控制不住的感情波动。
violent: 普通用词，指人时侧重极为不安，异常激，暗含有达或暴力行为；也指破坏性的或不可控制的自然力量。
brutal, ruthless, savage, fierce, inhuman, barbarous, cruel
这组词都有“残忍的”的意思，其区别是：
brutal: 指极端的残忍，强调无情或缺乏同情心，含不择手段的意味。
ruthless: 与cruel同义。强调为达到目的，对别人的痛苦毫无怜悯之心。
savage: 指缺乏文明人应有的教养，尤指在动怒或冲动时表现出的粗野蛮横，含野蛮意味。
fierce: 指天性凶恶，令人害怕。
inhuman: 着重缺乏同情心、仁爱等人类特有的良好的品质。
barbarous: 专指只有原始或未开化的人才会有的残忍行为。
cruel: 一般用词，指行动或态度的残忍。
adj. 凶猛的；猛烈的；暴躁的
- fell, violent, hard

entries.meaning:
n.战斗；打架；斗志
vt.打架；对抗

After spiritual purification, he meets the demon in a thrilling fight.

details.title: 例句
details.text:
